subject: Latency SLA criteria, decision tree, and demo coordination
messages:
From: Tom Keller <tom.keller@veridian.ai>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: support@veridian.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial perf discovery — p95/p99 targets and streaming notes

Alex — thanks for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying asks so we can align the PoC:  

Summary / asks:  
- Target p95 end-to-end latency: 120ms for short requests (~64 tokens).
- Target p99: <= 400ms for the same envelope; we can tolerate higher p99 for long-tail >512 tokens.
- Throughput: baseline 250 qps steady-state, with bursts to 600 qps for 30s windows during peak hours.
- Streaming: we require chunked output with server-sent events; client expects a token every ~20–30ms during generation for short responses.
- Concurrency: our gateway will open up to 200 concurrent client connections, but only ~80 simultaneous active generation streams expected in steady-state.

We attached our SLO matrix and a short streaming test plan. Can Redwood confirm: 1) whether hosted API can meet p95/p99 targets for short requests, 2) recommended concurrency limits and batching guidance, and 3) fallback model behavior if a node is overloaded?

Thanks — let me know windows next week for a short follow-up demo.

—Tom
Director, Platform Engineering
Veridian Health

Attachments: veridian_slo_matrix.xlsx, streaming_test_plan.pdf

From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Tom Keller <tom.keller@veridian.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial perf discovery — p95/p99 targets and streaming notes

Tom — great speaking with you. Appreciate the detailed targets, that helps a lot. Recap and proposed next steps from Redwood:  

Quick recap:  
- p95 target 120ms (64 tokens), p99 target <=400ms — noted.
- Throughput steady 250 qps, burst to 600 qps for ~30s windows.
- Streaming: SSE token cadence ~20–30ms for short responses.
- Concurrency profile: gateway will present up to 200 connections, ~80 active streams steady-state.

Technical fit notes (high-level):  
- Hosted API: we can meet the p95 120ms envelope for 64-token short responses on our optimized runtime using the recommended model variant with disabled heavy decoding features. We’ll validate p99 under your burst profile.
- Batching: to hit cost/latency tradeoffs we suggest a max dynamic batching window of 6–8ms for the PoC and explicit routing for low-latency routes (no batching) for critical endpoints.
- Streaming: our server supports streaming via SSE and WebSocket. We’ll instrument KV-cache warmup to avoid first-token stalls and emit partial tokens as they arrive.
- Fallbacks: policy options — immediate fallback to a smaller quantized model, regional reroute, or queued slow-path. We’ll define a decision tree in the PoC.

Proposed next steps:  
1) Redwood runs a 48-hour smoke validation against the Veridian streaming test plan we received (we’ll use your SLO matrix as acceptance criteria).
2) Schedule a 60-min technical demo / test-run on Wed 2027-04-28 or Thu 2027-04-29 (your preference). Marcus (runtime) + Laura (solutions) will join.
3) Share a draft decision tree for overload/fallback behavior and a recommended concurrency cap for the hosted route.

Can you confirm preferred slot for the demo and whether you want us to run the validation against your staging endpoint or we spin up an identical traffic generator from Redwood?

Best — Alex
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial perf discovery — p95/p99 targets and streaming notes

Tom / Alex — quick technical addition from the runtime side before the demo:  

Notes:  
- KV cache warmup is critical for p95 on short requests; recommend a short preflight of common prefixes (we can provide a small script).
- For streaming cadence (~20–30ms token emission) we need to cap decode concurrency per GPU to ~12 active streams to preserve per-token latency on our current host config. That means at 80 active streams you should plan for 7–8 GPUs in Dedicated; hosted will shard streams across instances — we’ll map this in the PoC.
- Batching windows: start with 6ms, observe tail behavior for p99. If you see p99 degradation under burst, we can reduce batch window or isolate low-latency route with no batching.
- Fallback decision tree: prefer regional reroute -> small-quant model -> queueing slow-path; immediate drop only for safety-critical overloads.

I’ll bring a proposed decision tree diagram to the demo and a short list of commands to run the streaming preflight.

—Marcus
Senior Runtime Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai

Actions:

Regards — Alex
